{{Short description|English mathematician (1856–1929)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
[[File:M.J.M. Hill from Mansch, Medical World, 1906 Wellcome M0012788.jpg|thumb|M. J. M. Hill (1906)]]
'''Micaiah John Muller Hill''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] (1856–1929) was an English mathematician, known for [[Hill's spherical vortex]]<ref>{{cite journal|author=Hill, M. J. M.|title=On a Spherical Vortex|journal=[[Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A]]|year=1894|volume=185|pages=213–245|doi=10.1098/rsta.1894.0006|bibcode=1894RSPTA.185..213H|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|author=Zaroodny, Serge J.|title=REVISED THEORY OF VORTEX RINGS – A SIMPLIFIED REVIEW OF THE STATE OF THE ART, Interim Report on Task No. 01-S-065|date=April 1966|publisher=U. S. Army Ballistic Research Laboratories|url=http://apps.dtic.mil/dtic/tr/fulltext/u2/645931.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140514173823/http://www.dtic.mil/dtic/tr/fulltext/u2/645931.pdf|url-status=live|archive-date=14 May 2014}}</ref> and [[Hill tetrahedron|Hill's tetrahedra]].

He was born on 22 February 1856 in [[Berhampore]], [[Bengal]], India, the son of Revd. Samuel John Hill (1825–1881) and Leonora Josephina Muller (1833–1917).

Hill received a bachelor's degree in 1873 and an M.A. in 1876 from [[University College, London]]. In 1880–1884, he was a professor of mathematics at [[Mason Science College|Mason College]] (which later became [[Birmingham University]]). In 1891, he earned his Sc.D. from [[Cambridge University]]. From 1884 to 1907, he was Professor of Pure Mathematics at University College, London and from 1907 to 1923 Astor Professor of Mathematics, University of London.<ref>{{acad|id=HL875MJ|name=Hill, Micaiah John Muller}}</ref>

In 1894, Hill was elected [[Fellow of the Royal Society]]. In 1926 and 1927 he served as president of the [[Mathematical Association]].

Hill was one of the people to whom C. L. T. Griffith sent, in 1912, some of Ramanujan's work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.imsc.res.in/~rao/ramanujan/newnow/griffith.htm|title=Untitled Document|website=www.imsc.res.in|accessdate=Jan 5, 2021}}</ref>

He married Minnie Grace Tarbotton, daughter of [[Marriott Ogle Tarbotton]] at St Saviour's Church, Paddington on 21 December 1892.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=Marriages |url=https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/viewer/bl/0000176/18921231/028/0003 |newspaper=Nottinghamshire Guardian |location=England |date=31 December 1892 |access-date=8 August 2020 |via=British Newspaper Archive |url-access=subscription  }}</ref> 
His two sons were [[Roderic Hill]] and [[Geoffrey T. R. Hill]].
